questions.title: When is one integer-feasibility test sufficient?
questions.statement: For integers a,b,c,d with D=ad-bc nonzero, classify when for every integer p,q, D divides aq-cp implies an integer solution of ax+by=p, cx+dy=q. Reviewed proposed classification: gcd(|a|,|c|)=1.
questions.next_step: Formalise both directions of the unchanged universal criterion. Reuse separately checked finite construction evidence in attempt 0003 without treating it as a universal proof.
questions.acceptance: Both directions, signed and zero coefficients, determinant and gcd assumptions explicit; independent statement review, pinned proof replay and axiom audit; no assumptions inserted to force success.
questions.novelty: Elementary generalisation of established linear Diophantine theory; no novelty claim. Exact literature match not established; search was not exhaustive.
